Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 38, verses 1–11:

Explanation of the words:

Sad: This is one of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'a). It is written ص and read "Sad". Allah knows best what He means by it.

By the Qur'an, full of reminder: That is, I swear by the Qur'an, full of reminder, for through it Allah, exalted is He, is remembered. The matter is not as these disbelievers say, that the Prophet is a sorcerer, a poet and a liar.

Rather, those who disbelieve are in arrogance and opposition: That is, the people of Makkah are in self-conceit and in opposition to the Prophet and the believers, and in enmity. Therefore they said about the Messenger what they said, whereas in truth they know his innocence of what they attributed to him.

How many generations We destroyed before them: That is, We destroyed many of the past nations.

They called out, but it was no time for escape: That is, they cried out and sought help, but it was not the time for flight or deliverance.

And they wondered: That is, the people of Makkah did not take warning from them, and they wondered that there came to them a warner from among themselves, Muhammad ﷺ.

They said, "A sorcerer, a great liar": That is, because of the miraculous things he displayed and because of what he attributed to Allah of sending and revelation.

Has he made the gods into one God? That is, when he told them, "Say: There is no god but Allah," they said, "How can one God suffice all creation?"

Indeed, this is a astonishing thing: That is, making the gods one god is a strange matter.

And the eminent among them went off, saying, "Walk on": That is, they went out from the house of Abu Talib, where they had been gathered with the Prophet ﷺ and had heard from him his saying to them, "Say: There is no god but Allah."

Indeed, this is something that is intended: That is, this tawhid that is mentioned is a matter intended for us to carry out.

In the last religion: That is, the religion of Jesus, peace be upon him.

This is nothing but a fabrication: That is, this is nothing but invented falsehood.

Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us? That is, how could that be, when he is neither greater than us nor more noble?

Rather, they are in doubt about My reminder: That is, rather, they are in doubt about the Qur'an and the revelation, and therefore they said about the Messenger what they said.

Rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment: That is, they have not yet tasted My punishment, for had they tasted it they would not have denied, but would have believed, and faith would not benefit them then.

Or do they possess the treasuries of the mercy of your Lord, the Almighty, the Bestower? That is, of prophethood and other things, so that they might give to whom they wish and withhold from whom they wish.

Or do they have dominion over the heavens and the earth? That is, they do not have that.

Let them then ascend by the means: That is, the means that reach the heaven, so that they might bring revelation and confine it to whom they wish, or prevent the revelation sent down upon our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. But how could they do that?

A host there, routed, of the confederates: That is, they are a contemptible host in their denial of you, routed before you, and at Badr.

Of the confederates: That is, of the past nations that banded together against their messengers, and whom Allah destroyed.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: "Sad. By the Qur'an, full of reminder." As for "Sad," it is one of the letters of the alphabet, and the way of the early scholars regarding it is to say: Allah knows best what He means by it, for it is among the ambiguous (mutashabih) matters that must be believed in, and the matter of its meaning is left to the One who sent it down. We have mentioned more than once that these letters have served two benefits, and let whoever wishes to learn them among the noble readers seek them from the surahs that open with such letters, such as Ta-Sin, Alif-Lam-Mim.

As for His words, "And the Qur'an": it is the Book of Allah that was sent down upon Muhammad ﷺ. "Full of reminder": its meaning is admonition, for through it Allah, exalted is He, is remembered. The phrase is an oath which Allah swore by, saying, "And the Qur'an, full of reminder." The answer to the oath is omitted, its implied meaning being: the matter is not as these polytheists say, that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is a sorcerer, a poet and a liar. "Rather, those who disbelieve are in arrogance and opposition": that is, rather, they are in self-conceit, pride, dissension and enmity towards the Prophet ﷺ and the believers, and this led them to say about the Messenger what they said. Otherwise, they know with certainty that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the farthest of people from sorcery, poetry, lying and madness.

His words, "How many generations We destroyed before them": that is, many past nations We destroyed for their denial of their messengers. When the punishment came upon them, they cried out, calling for help, "but it was no time for escape": that is, the hour was not an hour of deliverance or flight. So why do the polytheists of Makkah not take warning from the likes of these? They did not take warning. "And they wondered that there came to them a warner from among themselves": one who warns them of Allah's punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and he is Muhammad ﷺ. "And the disbelievers said": that is, they did not take warning, they wondered, and they said about him ﷺ, "A sorcerer, a great liar." "Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a astonishing thing": that is, astonishing; how could one God suffice the servants? Indeed, this is a matter that is wondered at in the extreme, because they measured the unseen, which is Allah, the Exalted, by the seen, which is weak man, and so they fell into the most vile and ugly error.

His words, "And the eminent among them went off": and they were saying to one another, "Walk on, and be steadfast in your gods." "Indeed, this is something that is intended": that is, something to be carried out and enforced by us. They said this and what follows of speech when they had gathered with the Messenger ﷺ in the house of his uncle Abu Talib to negotiate with the Messenger concerning his call. When the Messenger ﷺ said to them, "Say: There is no god but Allah," they rose from the assembly and went off walking and saying what Allah, exalted is He, related of them: "Walk on, and be steadfast in your gods": that is, in their worship, so do not abandon them. "Indeed, this": that is, the call to "There is no god but Allah," "is a great thing intended to be carried out by us, for the benefit of others." "We have not heard of this" – that is, of tawhid – "in the last religion": that is, the final religion, which is what Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, brought. "This is nothing but a fabrication": that is, what Muhammad calls to is nothing but a lie that he invented, which was not sent down to him nor revealed to him.

They continued their speech, saying, "Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us?": that is, the Qur'an, "from among us," while he is neither older than us nor more noble in lineage than us. How could this be?

His words, "Rather, they are in doubt about My reminder": that is, the people were not ignorant of Muhammad's truthfulness in what he said or the soundness of his mind. What led them to this was their doubt about the Qur'an, and what it brings down of truth and calls to of guidance. This is the first and second point. "Rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment": for had they tasted Allah's punishment for their denial, they would not have denied. They will taste it, but on that day neither assent nor faith will benefit them.

His words, "Or do they possess the treasuries of the mercy of your Lord, the Almighty, the Bestower?": that is, rather, do they have the treasuries of your Lord's mercy, O our Messenger, the Almighty, the Exalted, the Bestower of abundant gifts, of prophethood and other things? If so, they could give to whom they wish and withhold from whom they wish. But do they have any share of the treasuries of your Lord's mercy? The answer is no. Then why do they deny Allah's gift to Muhammad of prophethood, revelation and messengership?

His words, "Or do they have dominion over the heavens and the earth and what is between them?": that is, rather, do they have dominion over the heavens and the earth and what lies between them? If this were theirs, "then let them ascend by the means," step after step, until they reach the seventh heaven and prevent the revelation sent down upon Muhammad ﷺ from his Lord, glorified and exalted is He. But from where could they have that, when they are the weak and contemptible? As Allah said of them: "A host there, routed, of the confederates": that is, a contemptible host among the confederates of falsehood and evil, routed there at Badr and on the day of the Conquest, by Allah's permission.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Allah, the Exalted, may swear by whatever He wills, unlike the servant, who swears only by his Lord, the Exalted.

2- Clarification of the arrogance and enmity towards the Prophet ﷺ that the polytheists had.

3- Clarification of the ignorance of the polytheists in their rejection of "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

4- The challenge of the Lord, the Exalted, to the polytheists, to demonstrate their incapacity and to call them to descend to the truth and accept it.

5- The Qur'an's reports of the unseen and its truthfulness in that.

6- Condemnation of the term "confederates" and its implication, since confederates bring no good.

By the Qur'an, full of reminder: That is, I swear by the Qur'an, full of reminder, for through it Allah, exalted is He, is remembered. The matter is not as these disbelievers say, that the Prophet is a sorcerer, a poet and a liar.

Rather, those who disbelieve are in arrogance and opposition: That is, the people of Makkah are in self-conceit and in opposition to the Prophet and the believers, and in enmity. Therefore they said about the Messenger what they said, whereas in truth they know his innocence of what they attributed to him.

How many generations We destroyed before them: That is, We destroyed many of the past nations.

They called out, but it was no time for escape: That is, they cried out and sought help, but it was not the time for flight or deliverance.

And they wondered: That is, the people of Makkah did not take warning from them, and they wondered that there came to them a warner from among themselves, Muhammad ﷺ.

They said, "A sorcerer, a great liar": That is, because of the miraculous things he displayed and because of what he attributed to Allah of sending and revelation.

Has he made the gods into one God? That is, when he told them, "Say: There is no god but Allah," they said, "How can one God suffice all creation?"

Indeed, this is a astonishing thing: That is, making the gods one god is a strange matter.

And the eminent among them went off, saying, "Walk on": That is, they went out from the house of Abu Talib, where they had been gathered with the Prophet ﷺ and had heard from him his saying to them, "Say: There is no god but Allah."

Indeed, this is something that is intended: That is, this tawhid that is mentioned is a matter intended for us to carry out.

In the last religion: That is, the religion of Jesus, peace be upon him.

This is nothing but a fabrication: That is, this is nothing but invented falsehood.

Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us? That is, how could that be, when he is neither greater than us nor more noble?

Rather, they are in doubt about My reminder: That is, rather, they are in doubt about the Qur'an and the revelation, and therefore they said about the Messenger what they said.

Rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment: That is, they have not yet tasted My punishment, for had they tasted it they would not have denied, but would have believed, and faith would not benefit them then.

Or do they possess the treasuries of the mercy of your Lord, the Almighty, the Bestower? That is, of prophethood and other things, so that they might give to whom they wish and withhold from whom they wish.

Or do they have dominion over the heavens and the earth? That is, they do not have that.

Let them then ascend by the means: That is, the means that reach the heaven, so that they might bring revelation and confine it to whom they wish, or prevent the revelation sent down upon our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. But how could they do that?

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 38, verses 12–20:

Explanation of the words:

*Kadhdhabat qablahum* (they denied before them): i.e., before these polytheists of Quraysh.

*Wa Fir'awnu dhu al-awtad* (and Pharaoh, possessor of the stakes): i.e., the one who had four stakes to which he would tie whoever he wished to torture.

*Wa ashab al-Ayka* (and the people of al-Ayka): i.e., the thicket; they were the people of Shu'ayb.

*In kullun illa kadhdhaba al-rusul* (each of them only denied the messengers): i.e., each one of them denied the messengers and did not believe them in what they called to.

*Fa-haqqa 'iqab* (so My punishment was due): i.e., My punishment against them became due.

*Sayhatan wahidatan* (one single blast): this is the blast of Israfil into the Trumpet.

*Ma laha min fawaq* (it will have no pause): i.e., it will have no respite or cessation until it destroys everything.

*Ajjil lana qitta* (hasten for us our portion): i.e., the record of our deeds, that we may see what You have prepared for us, since *al-qitt* means the book.

*Dha al-ayd* (possessor of strength): i.e., strength and firmness in obedience to Allah, the Exalted.

*Innahu awwab* (indeed he was one who turns back): i.e., one who returns to Allah in all his affairs.

*Bil-'ashiyyi wal-ishraq* (in the evening and at sunrise): i.e., in the evening after the afternoon prayer until sunset, and at ishraq, from sunrise until the rising of the forenoon (duha).

*Wal-tayru mahshurah lahu* (and the birds gathered to him): i.e., the birds were assembled.

*Wa atayna-hu al-hikmata wa fasl al-khitab* (and We gave him wisdom and decisive speech): i.e., We gave Dawud wisdom, which is correctness in matters and soundness in them, and decisive speech, which is understanding in judgment; among it is the rule that the claimant must provide proof and the one who denies must swear an oath.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context consoles the Prophet ﷺ and warns the polytheists, so that they might repent to Allah and return. Allah says: ﴿Before them denied the people of Nuh, and 'Ad, and Pharaoh, possessor of the stakes﴾, i.e., the possessor of the stakes to which he would tie whoever he wanted to torture, torturing them upon them like the wooden gallows posts; ﴿and Thamud, and the people of Lut, and the companions of al-Ayka﴾, i.e., the thicket, the dense trees, and they were the people of Shu'ayb; ﴿those are the confederates﴾, i.e., the disbelieving, destroyed factions; ﴿each of them only denied the messengers﴾, i.e., not one of them did anything but deny the messengers; ﴿so My punishment was due﴾, i.e., My punishment against them became due, so I punished them. These people of your nation await only ﴿one single blast, with no pause﴾, i.e., no lull or cessation, until everything is destroyed and nothing remains except the Face of your Lord, Full of Majesty and Honour. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they said, "Our Lord, hasten for us our portion before the Day of Reckoning"﴾, they said this when the verses were revealed: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand﴾ [v. 19] and the following verses of Surah al-Haqqah. The extreme disbelievers, such as Abu Jahl and others, said it mockingly: "Our Lord, hasten for us our portion," i.e., our book, that we may see what is in it of good deeds and bad deeds before the Day of Resurrection, reckoning and recompense, while they did not believe in resurrection or recompense; they said this only as mockery and obstinacy or arrogance. Therefore Allah said to His Messenger: ﴿Be patient over what they say, and remember Our servant Dawud, possessor of strength﴾, i.e., strength in the religion of Allah, ﴿indeed he was one who turns back﴾, i.e., one who returns to Allah, the Exalted. Mention him so that you may take him as an example in his patience and his strength in the truth. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed We subjected [the mountains]﴾ and the following verses, it explains Allah's favour upon Dawud, so that the desire to follow him and the longing for Allah's bounties that are with Him may be greatly intensified: ﴿Indeed We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] with him in the evening and at sunrise﴾, i.e., when Dawud glorified Allah in the evening after the afternoon prayer until sunset, and at ishraq, which is the time of duha, the mountains glorified [Allah] with him, i.e., they echoed his glorification as an honour to him; ﴿and the birds gathered﴾, i.e., We subjected the birds, gathered, i.e., assembled, repeating the glorification with him. As for His saying, ﴿all of them were oft-returning to Him﴾, i.e., each of the mountains and birds was one who returns, glorifying Allah, the Exalted.

And His saying: ﴿And We strengthened his kingdom﴾, i.e., We strengthened the kingdom of Dawud by granting him all the means of material and spiritual strength. ﴿And We gave him wisdom﴾, which is prophethood, correctness in matters and soundness in them, whether in speech or in action. ﴿And decisive speech﴾, i.e., good judgment and insight in it, and sufficient clarity in his speech. So follow his example, O our Messenger.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Consolation of the Messenger ﷺ and encouraging him to be patient over the harm and denial of Quraysh and their obstinacy.

2- A warning to Quraysh that, if they persist in denial, they will face the most severe kinds of punishment.

3- Clarification of the mockery and contempt of the polytheists toward Allah's reports and His laws.

4- The legitimacy of taking the righteous as models and examples.

5- Explanation of the sign of Allah subjecting the mountains and birds to Dawud, glorifying Allah with him.

6- The beauty of Dawud's voice in his recitation and glorification.

7- The legitimacy of the ishraq and duha prayers.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 38, verses 21–25:

Explanation of the words:

"Has the news reached you?": the interrogative here is for wonder, that is, to prompt the addressee to be amazed.

"The news of the adversaries": that is, the report of the two litigants, strange in its circumstances and wondrous in its occurrence.

"When they climbed over the wall of the prayer chamber": that is, the prayer chamber of his place of worship, when they were prevented from entering by the door, so they came to its wall and descended from above the wall.

"One of us has wronged the other": that is, one of us has transgressed against the other.

"Judge between us with truth and do not exceed the bounds": that is, judge with justice and do not deviate in your judgment.

"And guide us to the even path": that is, guide us to justice in this case of ours, and do not incline us toward anything other than the truth.

"This is my brother": that is, in religion, in Islam.

"Give him to me": that is, make me its guardian, meaning, cede it to me and transfer its ownership to me.

"And he has overpowered me in speech": that is, he prevailed over me in argumentative speech and took it from me.

"He has certainly wronged you by demanding your ewe be added to his ewes": that is, by his request for your ewe and his adding it to his ewes.

"Indeed, many associates oppress one another": that is, partners wrong one another.

"And David realized that We had tried him": that is, David became certain that his Lord had tested him, that is, examined him.

"So he asked forgiveness of his Lord and fell down in prostration and turned in repentance": that is, he sought forgiveness from his Lord by saying "I seek forgiveness from Allah," and fell prostrate on the ground, and "turned in repentance" means he returned repentant to his Lord.

"And indeed, he has near access to Us and a good return": that is, a good place of return with Us, and this is Paradise and its high ranks.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to console the Messenger and to strengthen him to endure the insolence and harm he suffers from the disbelievers of Quraysh. So his Lord, exalted is He, said to him, ﴿Has the news reached you?﴾ up to the end of the verses. This is because David, peace be upon him, once reflected within himself on what Allah, exalted is He, had honored Abraham, Isaac and Jacob with, namely the lasting good praise among people, so he wished for the like of it. It was said to him that they had been tested and had been patient, so he asked to be tried as they had been tried and to be given as they had been given, if he should be patient. So Allah, exalted is He, tested him in accordance with his desire. He sent to him two angels in the form of two men, and they climbed over his prayer chamber, as its detailed account will come in the verses. This is His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Has the news reached you?﴾ O our Messenger, of the news of the adversaries, and they were two angels in the form of two men. The word "khasm" (adversary) is applied to the singular and the plural, as with "'adu" (enemy); one says "this is my adversary" and "these are my adversary," and "this is my enemy" and "these are an enemy to me." His saying ﴿when they climbed over the prayer chamber﴾ means they ascended over the wall of the dwelling that is the prayer chamber in the custom of the Children of Israel, and they did not enter by the door, because the guards prevented them from doing so, since David had a time in which he was devoted to worship, and so no one was permitted to meet him. His saying ﴿when they entered upon David and he was startled by them﴾ means he was alarmed and his soul was disturbed. ﴿They said: Fear not; two adversaries﴾ meaning, we are two adversaries ﴿one of us has wronged the other﴾ meaning, one of us has transgressed against the other; we have come to have you judge between us ﴿so judge between us with truth and do not exceed the bounds﴾ meaning, do not deviate in judgment ﴿and guide us to the even path﴾ meaning, to the middle of the way, so do not turn us away from the truth.

Then we presented the case to him, and one of them, the wronged party, stated his grievance: ﴿Indeed, this is my brother﴾ meaning in religion ﴿he has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe, and he said: Give it to me﴾ meaning, make it mine; I will add it to my ewes. ﴿And he has overpowered me in speech﴾ meaning, he prevailed over me in speech and argument and took it from me. David then judged at once, without having heard from the second adversary: ﴿He has certainly wronged you by demanding your ewe be added to his ewes.﴾ He justified this by saying ﴿And indeed, many associates oppress one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ meaning, partners in crops, livestock or trade ﴿and few are they﴾ meaning, they are very few. Here the two angels flew away from before David's eyes and ascended to heaven. Then he knew that his Lord had tested him, as he had desired, and that he had not been patient, since he had judged without hearing from the second adversary. It was a small slip, which showed him that what Abraham, Isaac and Jacob had attained of perfection was the result of a great trial. Here David asked his Lord for forgiveness ﴿and fell down prostrate﴾ weeping and seeking pardon, and turned in repentance to his Lord in all his affairs. Allah, exalted is He, mentioned that He accepted his repentance and pardoned him, saying, exalted is He, ﴿So We forgave him that; and indeed, for him with Us is near access and a good return﴾ meaning, because of his nearness to Us ﴿and a good return﴾ meaning, a place of return, which is the high ranks in the abode of the righteous. May Allah, exalted is He, make us among its people by His grace and mercy.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The benefit of relating such stories is to strengthen the heart of the Messenger ﷺ, to make his heart firm, and to bring him to patience.

2- Confirmation of the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ, since such a story cannot be related by him except through divine revelation.

3- Confirmation of the permissibility of angels appearing in the form of human beings.

4- The prohibition for a judge or ruler to issue a judgment before hearing the claim from both litigants together, since this is the place of the trial that befell David, peace be upon him.

5- The obligation of repentance upon falling into sin.

6- The legitimacy of prostration upon reciting this verse, ﴿and fell down prostrate and turned in repentance﴾.

The context continues to console the Messenger and to strengthen him to endure the insolence and harm he suffers from the disbelievers of Quraysh. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 38, verses 26–29:

Explanation of the words:

*Inna ja'alnaka khalifah* (Indeed, We have made you a successor): i.e., you succeed those who came before you in managing the affairs of the people by Our permission.

*Wa la tattabi' al-hawa* (And do not follow desire): i.e., the desire of the self, which is what it inclines to and craves.

*Fa-yudillaka 'an sabil Allah* (so that it leads you astray from the path of Allah): i.e., from the way that leads to His good pleasure.

*Inna alladhina yadilluna 'an sabil Allah* (Indeed, those who go astray from the path of Allah): i.e., who miss the way that leads to His good pleasure, which is faith and God-consciousness (taqwa).

*Bima nasu yawm al-hisab* (for that they forgot the Day of Reckoning): i.e., because of their forgetting the Day of Resurrection, so they did not fear Allah, exalted is He.

*Batilan* (in vain): i.e., in vain, without a wise purpose intended in that creation.

*Dhalika zann alladhina kafaru* (That is the assumption of those who disbelieve): i.e., the assumption that the heavens and the earth and what is between them were created in vain, without a purpose intended by it, is the assumption of those who disbelieve.

*Fa-wayl lilladhina kafaru min al-nar* (So woe to those who disbelieve, from the Fire): i.e., from a valley in the Fire whose depth is far and whose smell is foul, unbearable.

*Mubarak* (blessed): i.e., blessing never departs from it; its reader, its practitioner, and its judge find it.

*Liyatadhakkara ulu al-albab* (that those of sound intellect may take heed): i.e., that people of sound and discerning minds may be admonished by it.

Meaning of the verses:

The discussion continues concerning the story of Dawud (David), for admonition and reflection, and for strengthening the heart of the Prophet (ﷺ). Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿O Dawud﴾, i.e., and We said to him, after his repentance and its acceptance: O Dawud, ﴿Indeed, We have made you a successor upon the earth﴾, succeeding those prophets who came before you, managing the affairs of the people. ﴿So judge between the people in truth﴾, i.e., with justice that accords with the law of Allah and His pleasure, ﴿and do not follow desire﴾, which is what your self desires apart from what is the law of Allah. ﴿For it will lead you astray﴾, i.e., following desire will lead you astray from the path of Allah, which leads the servants to felicity and perfection. This is because, when rulings conform to the divine Shari'ah, the interests of the servants are ordered by them and benefit both the common people and the elite; but when rulings follow desire and the ruler's pursuit of the aims of his own self alone, they lead to the ruin of the world through the occurrence of chaos and turmoil among the people, and in that is the destruction of both the ruler and the ruled. And His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, those who go astray from the path of Allah﴾, those who depart from faith, God-consciousness, and the establishment of the Shari'ah and justice, ﴿for them is a severe punishment, for that they forgot the Day of Reckoning﴾, i.e., because of their forgetting the Day of Resurrection, so they abandoned working for it, which is faith and God-consciousness: God-consciousness being the performance of the divine commands and avoidance of the prohibitions in belief, speech, and action.

His saying, exalted is He, in verse [27]: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain﴾. Exalted is He, He negates what the polytheists assume, namely that the creation of the universe had no wisdom that necessitated its creation and origination, which is that Allah be worshipped through His remembrance and gratitude, embodied in faith and God-consciousness. And His saying: ﴿That is the assumption of those who disbelieve﴾, i.e., the assumption that Allah created the heaven and the earth and what is between them without an intended purpose, which is the worship of Allah through the heart-based, verbal, and physical acts of worship He has prescribed for His servants: the assumption of those who disbelieve, from the disbelievers of Makkah and others. Then He threatened them for their disbelief and their erroneous assumption which resulted in their disbelief and disobedience, saying: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire﴾, i.e., woe to those who disbelieve, from a valley in Hell whose depth is far and whose smell is foul.

His saying, exalted is He, in verse [28]: ﴿Shall We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like the corrupters in the earth? Or shall We treat the righteous like the wicked?﴾ This is, firstly, a refutation of what the polytheists claimed, that they would receive in the Hereafter the same bliss that the believers receive. Secondly, He, exalted is He, negates that He equates those who believe in Him and follow His guidance, obeying Him in His commands and prohibitions, with those who corrupt the earth through polytheism and sins, just as He negates that He makes the righteous who believe and are God-conscious, who abandon polytheism and sins, like the wicked (*fujjar*), who deviated, i.e., departed from the obedience of Allah and His Messenger, so they did not believe nor affirm the Oneness of Allah, and lived as disbelievers and wicked persons and died upon that. That is: far removed is Allah, Lord of the worlds, the most just of the just and the wisest of the judges, from equating the people of faith and God-consciousness with the people of polytheism and sins; rather He grants bliss to the former in the abode of delight, and punishes the latter in the midst of the Blazing Fire.

His saying, exalted is He, in verse [29]: ﴿A Book which We have sent down to you﴾, i.e., this is a blessed Book which We have sent down upon Our Messenger, that they may ponder its verses, meaning contemplate them and reflect upon them with their intellects, so that they attain guidance of hearts and minds, believe in Allah, and act in obedience to Him, so that they are saved and made happy. ﴿That those of sound intellect may take heed﴾, i.e., that those of sound minds may be admonished by its exhortations and restrained by its warnings. Describing the Book, which is the Qur'an, with blessing, is as Allah has informed: blessing never departs from the Qur'an, and it is goodness that endures. Whoever recites it reflectively comes to know guidance; whoever recites it seeking nearness attains nearness and succeeds by it; and whoever recites it as a judge rules justly in his judgment.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The obligation to judge with justice upon everyone who judges, and there is no justice outside the divine law.

2- The prohibition of following desire, since it leads the servant to ruin and loss.

3- The affirmation of resurrection and recompense.

4- The refutation of the assumption of one who thinks that the worldly life was created in vain and without purpose.

5- The exaltation of the Lord, exalted is He, above vanity and injustice.

6- The excellence of intellects for one who uses them in reflection and remembrance.

7- The blessing of the Qur'an never departs from it, and no one sought it without finding it.

And His saying: ﴿That is the assumption of those who disbelieve﴾, i.e., the assumption that Allah created the heaven and the earth and what is between them without an intended purpose, which is the worship of Allah through the heart-based, verbal, and physical acts of worship He has prescribed for His servants: the assumption of those who disbelieve, from the disbelievers of Makkah and others. Then He threatened them for their disbelief and their erroneous assumption which resulted in their disbelief and disobedience, saying: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire﴾, i.e., woe to those who disbelieve, from a valley in Hell whose depth is far and whose smell is foul.

His saying, exalted is He, in verse [28]: ﴿Shall We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like the corrupters in the earth? Or shall We treat the righteous like the wicked?﴾ This is, firstly, a refutation of what the polytheists claimed, that they would receive in the Hereafter the same bliss that the believers receive. Secondly, He, exalted is He, negates that He equates those who believe in Him and follow His guidance, obeying Him in His commands and prohibitions, with those who corrupt the earth through polytheism and sins, just as He negates that He makes the righteous who believe and are God-conscious, who abandon polytheism and sins, like the wicked (*fujjar*), who deviated, i.e., departed from the obedience of Allah and His Messenger, so they did not believe nor affirm the Oneness of Allah, and lived as disbelievers and wicked persons and died upon that. That is: far removed is Allah, Lord of the worlds, the most just of the just and the wisest of the judges, from equating the people of faith and God-consciousness with the people of polytheism and sins; rather He grants bliss to the former in the abode of delight, and punishes the latter in the midst of the Blazing Fire.

Whoever recites it reflectively comes to know guidance; whoever recites it seeking nearness attains nearness and succeeds by it; and whoever recites it as a judge rules justly in his judgment.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The obligation to judge with justice upon everyone who judges, and there is no justice outside the divine law.

2- The prohibition of following desire, since it leads the servant to ruin and loss.

3- The affirmation of resurrection and recompense.

4- The refutation of the assumption of one who thinks that the worldly life was created in vain and without purpose.

5- The exaltation of the Lord, exalted is He, above vanity and injustice.

6- The excellence of intellects for one who uses them in reflection and remembrance.

7- The blessing of the Qur'an never departs from it, and no one sought it without finding it.

*Fa-yudillaka 'an sabil Allah* (so that it leads you astray from the path of Allah): i.e., from the way that leads to His good pleasure.

*Inna alladhina yadilluna 'an sabil Allah* (Indeed, those who go astray from the path of Allah): i.e., who miss the way that leads to His good pleasure, which is faith and God-consciousness (taqwa).

*Bima nasu yawm al-hisab* (for that they forgot the Day of Reckoning): i.e., because of their forgetting the Day of Resurrection, so they did not fear Allah, exalted is He.

*Batilan* (in vain): i.e., in vain, without a wise purpose intended in that creation.

*Dhalika zann alladhina kafaru* (That is the assumption of those who disbelieve): i.e., the assumption that the heavens and the earth and what is between them were created in vain, without a purpose intended by it, is the assumption of those who disbelieve.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 38, verses 30–33:

Explanation of the words:

"And We gave to Dawud (David) Sulayman (Solomon)": That is, among Our gifts to Dawud the penitent, We gave him Sulayman, his son.

"What an excellent servant! Indeed, he was ever turning back (to Allah)": That is, Sulayman turned back to his Lord in repentance and devotion.

"Al-safinat al-jiyad (the poised, swift steeds)": That is, the horses standing on three legs, the swift ones, the racers.

"Hubb al-khayr (love of good)": That is, love of the horses, which distracted him from the remembrance of my Lord, and it was the afternoon prayer ('asr), because he was occupied with reviewing the horses for jihad.

"Until they were hidden behind the veil": That is, the sun set on the horizon and was covered from the eyes of onlookers.

"Bring them back to me": That is, bring back the horses I had just reviewed, which had distracted me from the remembrance of my Lord.

"Then he began to pass his hand over their legs and necks": That is, he began to stroke the legs and necks of those horses.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the discussion of Allah's bounty upon Dawud, where He says, "And We gave to Dawud Sulayman; what an excellent servant." He, exalted is He, mentions that He gave him Sulayman and praised Sulayman as an excellent servant of Allah. He gave the reason for this preference by saying, "Indeed, he was ever turning back (to Allah)," meaning one who frequently returns to Allah Most High. This turning back is returning to Allah by remembering Him and seeking His forgiveness when heedlessness or forgetfulness overtakes the servant. Allah Most High alluded to this in His words, "When there were displayed before him, at the evening time, the poised, swift steeds," meaning the horses strong in their running, which, when they stand, refuse to stand on four legs like donkeys but stand on three, raising the fourth; and al-jiyad are those swift in their running. This display was a review he conducted of them in preparation for a campaign he intended, so he reviewed his horses and was occupied with that until he failed to notice the afternoon prayer, and he realized nothing until the sun had set, which is the meaning of the words of the Most High:

"Until they were hidden behind the veil": That is, the sun was concealed "behind the veil," meaning the horizon, which screened it from the eyes of onlookers. He regretted that and said, "Indeed, I have preferred the love of good," meaning the horses, "over the remembrance of my Lord," and he prayed the afternoon prayer. Then he returned to completing the review, so his men brought the horses back to him, and he began to pass his hand over their legs and necks until he had completed their review. This is the aspect of turning back for which Sulayman, peace be upon him, was described in the words of the Most High, "Indeed, he was ever turning back."

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- A righteous child is a divine gift to his father, so one should thank Allah Most High for the One who granted it.

2- Praise of a servant for immediate repentance that follows a sin directly.

3- The permissibility of a ruler or commander reviewing his forces to inspect them for whatever may have arisen among them.

4- Applying the word "good" to horses affirms that horses, when tethered in the cause of Allah, their food and drink become good deeds for the one who tethers them in the cause of Allah, as in the authentic hadith, "Horses are for three..."

5- Tethering jet aircraft in hangars today, and armored vehicles and preparing them for battle in the cause of Allah, takes the place of tethering horses in the cause of Allah.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 38, verses 34–40:

Explanation of the words:

"And We did tempt Solomon" (وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا سُلَيْمَانَ): i.e., We tested him.

"And We placed upon his throne a body" (وَأَلْقَيْنَا عَلَىٰ كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَدًا): i.e., a split-off child, dead and without a soul in it.

"Then he turned back" (ثُمَّ أَنَابَ): i.e., he returned to his Lord and repented to Him for not making an exception (istithna', saying "God willing") in his oath.

"Grant me a kingdom that shall not befit anyone after me" (وَهَبْ لِي مُلْكًا لَا يَنبَغِي لِأَحَدٍ مِّن بَعْدِي): i.e., give me a kingdom that will not belong to anyone other than me among mankind.

"So We subjected to him the wind" (فَسَخَّرْنَا لَهُ الرِّيحَ): i.e., We responded to him, so We subjected the wind to him, running at his command.

"Gently, wherever he directed it" (رُخَاءً حَيْثُ أَصَابَ): i.e., mild wherever he willed.

"And the devils, every builder and diver" (وَالشَّيَاطِينَ كُلَّ بَنَّاءٍ وَغَوَّاصٍ): i.e., We subjected to him the devils among the jinn, some of them builders and some of them divers in the sea.

"Bound together in shackles" (مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي الْأَصْفَادِ): i.e., bound in shackles, their hands tied to their necks, in dark prisons; this was when they rebelled and disobeyed one of his commands.

"This is Our gift" (هَٰذَا عَطَاؤُنَا): i.e., and We said to him, "This is Our gift."

"So bestow or withhold" (فَامْنُنْ أَوْ أَمْسِكْ): i.e., give to whom you will and what you will, and withhold likewise.

"Without reckoning" (بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ): i.e., without any account from Us to you.

"And indeed for him with Us is nearness" (وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِندَنَا لَزُلْفَىٰ): i.e., and indeed for Solomon with Us is a station of nearness on the Day of Resurrection.

"And a good return" (وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ): i.e., a place of return in Paradise, in the highest ranks.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the mention of God's favours upon the family of David. Here God informs us of what He bestowed upon Solomon: He informs us that He tested him just as He tested his father David, and that Solomon repented just as David repented, and that this did not diminish their high rank or the nobility of their station. God says in verse [34]: ﴿And We did tempt Solomon﴾, i.e., We tested him. This is because the Messenger of God (ﷺ) reported in the authentic collection that he said: "I will surely go in to a hundred women tonight, and each woman will bear a child who will grow up to be a horseman fighting in the way of God," and he did not say "if God wills" (in shā' Allāh), i.e., he made no exception. He had relations with his wives that night, and he was punished for not making the exception: none of them gave birth except one, who bore a child paralysed by hemiplegia. When his mother delivered him, they brought him to Solomon and placed him upon his throne. This is His saying: ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body; then he turned back﴾, meaning Solomon turned to his Lord, sought forgiveness and repented, so God accepted his repentance. He said: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that shall not befit anyone after me﴾, i.e., that there be no one like it among mankind other than me. He sought nearness to God in having his supplication accepted by saying: ﴿Indeed You are the Bestower﴾. God answered him and subjected the wind to him, running at his command wherever he wished, for it would carry his carpet or his aerial ship, whose morning journey was a month's travel and whose evening journey was likewise, and it blew gently (rukhā'), i.e., mild wherever he directed it. He also subjected to him the devils of the jinn: some of them were builders who constructed houses and workshops, and some were divers who worked in the sea extracting pearls. And whoever of them disobeyed and rebelled against him, he gathered his hands to his neck with a shackle and placed him under the earth. This is what God said: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running at his command, gently, wherever he directed; and the devils, every builder and diver, and others bound together in shackles﴾, and His saying: ﴿This is Our gift, so bestow or withhold without reckoning﴾, i.e., We gave him what he asked of Us, and We said to him, "This is Our gift to you; so bestow what you will upon whom you will, and withhold what you will from whom you will, without any reckoning from Us against you."

Beyond this, indeed for you with Us on the Day of Resurrection is nearness and a good return. This is His saying: ﴿And indeed for him with Us is nearness and a good return﴾.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 38, verses 41–44:

Explanation of the words:

Wadhkur ʿabdana Ayyub (﴿وَٱذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَآ أيُّوبَ﴾): That is: O our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), remember Our servant Ayyub, son of ʿIs (Esau) son of Ishaq son of Ibrahim.

Bi-nusbin wa-ʿadhab: That is, with harm and severe pain. He attributed this to Shaytan because he was the cause, and out of courtesy toward Allah the Exalted.

Ir-kud bi-rijlika: That is, strike the earth with your foot, and a spring of water will gush forth.

Hadha mughtasalun barid wa-sharab: That is, We said to him: This is cool water; bathe in it and drink from it, and you will be healed.

Dighthan: That is, a bundle of dry grass.

Wa-la tahnath: By not striking her with it.

Ni'ma al-ʿabd: That is, Ayyub (peace be upon him).

Innahu awwab: That is, one who returns repeatedly to Allah the Exalted.

The meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the stories of the prophets, to strengthen the heart of His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). So the Exalted said to him: ﴿And remember Our servant Ayyub﴾, namely Ayyub son of ʿIs son of Ishaq son of Ibrahim the Friend, peace be upon them, ﴿when he called out to his Lord﴾, that is, he called upon Him saying: ﴿"Indeed, Shaytan has touched me with hardship and torment"﴾, that is, severe pain, and that was after a severe illness that lasted for a period of more than so many years. And in another supplication, mentioned in Surah al-Anbiya', he said to his Lord: ﴿"Indeed, harm has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful"﴾ [21:83]. The Exalted said: ﴿So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of harm, and We gave him his family and the like of them with them﴾ [21:84]. And His saying: ﴿"Strike with your foot; this is a cool bath and drink"﴾, that is, when Allah wished to remove the harm from him, He said to him: strike with your foot, that is, strike the earth with your foot, and water will gush from it; drink from it and bathe, and you will be healed. He did so, and he was healed as if no harm had ever been upon him at all. And His saying the Exalted: ﴿And We gave him his family and the like of them with them﴾, that is, Allah the Exalted compensated him for the family and children he had lost. And His saying: ﴿As a mercy from Us﴾, that is, that compensation was a mercy from Us to Ayyub. ﴿And a reminder for those of understanding﴾, that is, a lesson for people of living, aware hearts, by which they know that Allah may test the dearest of His servants so that by it He raises them to lofty ranks that they could not reach without being tested for the sake of Allah and being patient with it. And His saying: ﴿And take in your hand a bundle﴾, that is, We said to him: take in your hand a bundle, that is, a bundle of dry grass, and strike with it your wife one blow, for the bundle contains a hundred stalks. He had sworn that he would strike his wife a hundred lashes because of a shortcoming she had committed on one day of their life together, so his Lord the Exalted gave him the ruling mentioned in this verse. And His saying the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We found him patient﴾, that is, We tested him with illness, the loss of family, wealth and children, and We found him patient. For this He praised him by saying: ﴿How excellent a servant﴾, that is, Ayyub, ﴿Indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned back﴾, returning to his Lord in every matter, knowing none but Allah.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The affirmation of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) through this narrative, which could only be known through divine revelation.

2- Allah the Exalted may test those of His servants whom He loves, in order to increase the loftiness of their station and the elevation of their rank.

3- The virtue of patience and its praiseworthy outcome in this world and the Hereafter.

4- The legitimacy of issuing legal opinions (fatwa), which is specific to people of jurisprudence and knowledge.

5- The obligation of expiation (kaffara) upon one who breaks his oath.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 38, verses 45–54:

Explanation of the words:

"And remember Our servants": that is, remember their patience in the face of what befell them, for you have in them an example (uswa).

"Men of power (ulii al-aydi)": that is, those possessing strength in worship.

"And of insight (al-absar)": that is, insight in religion through knowing its secrets and wisdoms.

"With a pure (khalisa) thing": that is, it is the remembrance of the Final Abode and working for it.

"Of the chosen and excellent (al-mustafin al-akhyar)": that is, of those chosen and excellent, the plural of khayyir.

"This is a remembrance": that is, for them, with a fine and beautiful praise here in this world.

"And indeed for the God-fearing (al-muttaqin)": that is, they and others from among all the believing men and women.

"A good return (husna ma'ab)": that is, a place of return, when they return to their Lord by death.

"Reclining therein": that is, upon couches (al-arai'k).

This is the commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 38, verses 55–64:

**Explanation of the words:**

*Hadha* (this): i.e., what has been mentioned for the righteous.

*Wa inna lil-taghin* (And indeed for the transgressors): i.e., those who transgressed in disbelief, evil and corruption.

*Lasharra ma'ab* (the worst place of return): i.e., Jahannam (Hell), which they will burn in.

*Fa-bi'sa al-mihad* (and how evil is the resting-place): i.e., the bed which they prepared for themselves in the world through shirk (associating partners with Allah) and sins.

*Hadha fa-l-yadhuquhu* (This, so let them taste it): i.e., the punishment understood from what follows, so let them taste it.

*Hamim* (boiling water): i.e., scalding hot water that burns.

*Ghassaq* (dripping pus): i.e., pus and matter flowing from the flesh and private parts of adulterers in the Fire.

*Wa akhar min shaklihi azwaj* (and other punishments of similar kind): i.e., other punishments of the same kind as the boiling water and the ghassaq, in various types.

*Hadha fawjun muqtahimun ma'akum* (This is a troop rushing in with you): i.e., it will be said to them upon their entry into the Fire: "This is a troop rushing in with you."

*La marhaban bihim* (No welcome for them): i.e., no spaciousness upon them and no comfort for them; indeed they are destined to burn in the Fire.

*Qalu* (They say), i.e., the followers to the transgressors: "Nay, but you — no welcome to you! You brought this upon us."

*Qalu rabbana man qaddama lana hadha* (They say: Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us): i.e., the followers say: whoever was the cause of this punishment of ours in Hell, then increase his punishment.

*Wa qalu ma lana la nara rijalan* (And they say: What is wrong with us that we do not see men): i.e., the transgressors, while in the Fire, say: "What is wrong with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the wicked in the world?", meaning the poor Muslims such as Bilal, 'Ammar and Suhayb.

*Attakhadhnahum sikhriyya* (We used to take them for mockery): i.e., we used to mock them in the world.

*Am zaghat 'anhumu al-absar* (Or have our eyes turned away from them?): i.e., are they lost, or have our eyes turned away from them so that we do not see them?

*Inna dhalika la-haqqun takhasumu ahli al-nar* (Indeed that is true: the dispute of the people of the Fire): i.e., indeed that which has been mentioned of the people of the Fire is a established truth, namely the dispute of the people of the Fire.

**Meaning of the verses:**

After mentioning the bliss of the people of faith and piety, it was fitting to mention the wretchedness of the people of disbelief and wickedness, which is the method of warning and encouragement distinctive to the Noble Qur'an in guiding the servants. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿This is so.﴾ i.e., what has preceded of the bliss of the people of felicity. ﴿And indeed for the transgressors﴾ who are the polytheists and wrongdoers such as Abu Jahl, 'Utba ibn Mu'ayt and al-'As ibn Wa'il, ﴿there is an evil place of return﴾ i.e., the worst and most loathsome destination, which is ﴿Jahannam, they will burn in it, and how evil is the resting-place﴾; it is a bed that the wrongdoers prepared for themselves. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿This, so let them taste it: boiling water and dripping pus﴾ i.e., this is boiling water and dripping pus, so let them taste it. The hamim is scalding water that burns, and the ghassaq is what flows from the skins, flesh and private parts of the adulterers among the people of the Fire, such as pus and matter. His saying ﴿And other punishments of similar kind﴾ i.e., and another punishment of the same kind as the first, ﴿in various types.﴾ His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿This is a troop rushing in with you﴾ i.e., it will be said upon their entry into the Fire: this is a company, i.e., a group, rushing into the Fire with you. The transgressors will say, ﴿No welcome to them﴾ i.e., no spaciousness and no comfort for them, ﴿indeed they are destined to burn in the Fire﴾ i.e., they will enter it, burnt by its heat and flame. The followers will answer them saying, ﴿Nay, but you — no welcome to you!﴾ i.e., no spaciousness and no comfort, ﴿you brought this upon us﴾ since you used to command us to shirk, disbelief and wickedness. Allah said: ﴿They say: "Evil is the abode"﴾ i.e., the final place reached by the transgressors and their followers in the Fire. They also said what Allah reported of them in His saying: ﴿They say: "Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us — then increase him in punishment double in the Fire."﴾ i.e., O our Lord, double the punishment for them, for they are the ones who brought it upon us on the day they used to call us to shirk and falsehood and urged us toward it.

His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And they say﴾ i.e., the tyrants, ﴿What is wrong with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the wicked﴾ among us ﴿that we took them﴾ in the world ﴿as objects of mockery﴾ we used to ridicule, meaning the poor Muslims such as Bilal, 'Ammar, Suhayb and Khabbab. ﴿Are they missing, or have our eyes turned away from them?﴾ i.e., our sight failed to see them. Allah said: ﴿Indeed that is true: the dispute of the people of the Fire﴾ i.e., indeed that word which passed between the people of the Fire is true and sincere, it is the dispute of the people of the Fire. So hear it, O polytheists: today verses are recited, and tomorrow, the Day of Reckoning, will bring realities you will witness, bitter draughts you will swallow, and regrets that tear at livers and hearts.

**Guidance of the verses:**

1- Condemnation of tyranny, which is exceeding the limit in wrongdoing and disbelief, and a statement of the recompense of its people on the Day of Resurrection.

Al-'Aziz al-Ghaffar (the Mighty, the Forgiving): i.e., the Dominant who is not resisted in His will, the Forgiving of those who repent among His servants.

Qul huwa naba'un 'azim (Say: It is a mighty news): i.e., say, O Our Messenger, to the disbelievers of Makkah: the Qur'an is a mighty news and a momentous report.

Antum 'anhu mu'ridun (You turn away from it): you do not desire to hear it nor to reflect upon its meanings.

Bil-mala' al-a'la (of the Exalted Assembly): i.e., of the angels, when they disputed about the creation of Adam.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 38, verses 75–88:

Explanation of the words:

﴿What I created with My two hands﴾: i.e., for the one I created with My hands, who is Adam; this indicates his honour.

﴿Did you become arrogant, or were you of the haughty?﴾: i.e., have you become arrogant now, or were you among the arrogant ones before? The question is one of rebuke and reproach directed at Iblis.

﴿So get out of it﴾: i.e., out of Paradise.

﴿Indeed, you are accursed (rajim)﴾: i.e., stoned, expelled.

﴿And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense﴾: i.e., his expulsion from Paradise and the curse attached to him, which is removal from mercy, until the Day of Recompense (yawm al-din), that is, the Day of Resurrection.

﴿He said, "My Lord, then reprieve me﴾: i.e., delay my death and keep me alive ﴿until the Day they are resurrected﴾, i.e., the people.

﴿Until the day of the appointed time﴾: i.e., until the first blast, the blast of death and annihilation.

﴿Except Your sincere servants among them﴾: i.e., those whom You have chosen for belief in You, worship of You, and proximity to You in Paradise.

﴿Say, "I do not ask of you any payment for it﴾: I do not ask you for a reward in exchange for conveying the message that you would give me.

﴿And I am not of the pretentious﴾: i.e., those who fabricate the Qur'an, and I do not warn you with it of my own accord.

﴿It is not but a reminder to the worlds﴾: i.e., what I recite of the Qur'an and what I speak of guidance is nothing but a reminder to the worlds.

﴿And you will surely know its news after a time﴾: i.e., and you, O deniers, will surely come to know, after a time, the news of the Qur'an that it announced: the promise to the believers and the threat to the disbelievers.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the mention of what took place between the Lord, exalted is He, and His enemy Iblis, of a dialogue in the Highest Assembly, when, after Iblis refused to prostrate to Adam, the Exalted said: ﴿O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My two hands?﴾ meaning: what made you refrain from prostrating to Adam when I had commanded you to do so? ﴿Have you become arrogant?﴾ meaning: now? ﴿Or were you among the haughty?﴾ meaning: the arrogant ones. This question from God is a rebuke and reproach to Iblis. Iblis answered with what God related of him in His saying: ﴿He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."﴾ The accursed one used a corrupt analogy, rejected by people of sound intellect, for fire has never been better than clay: fire burns and its end is ash, whereas clay does not burn, and from it come all kinds of nourishing things by which life is sustained: grains, fruits, vegetables, and meats. It suffices that clay is the origin of man and the material of his creation. What greater nobility would fire have, if the accursed one had reason? Here God said to him: ﴿So get out of it﴾, i.e., out of Paradise, ﴿for indeed, you are accursed (rajim)﴾, i.e., expelled and removed, not fit to remain in the mercy of God, ﴿and indeed, upon you is My curse﴾ that will not leave you throughout life, which is distance from My mercy for the duration of life.

Here the accursed one, having despaired of mercy, said: ﴿My Lord, then reprieve me﴾, i.e., keep me alive and do not cause me to die, ﴿until the Day they are resurrected﴾, so that he may be able to seduce the children of Adam, and not die when they die at the first blast, so that he would not taste death himself. God knew what he concealed within himself, so He answered him with His saying: ﴿Indeed, you are among the reprieved﴾, i.e., those granted respite, whose lives are kept, ﴿until the Day of the appointed time﴾, which is the first blast, when he will die along with the rest of creation. When the accursed one knew that he had been granted respite, he said, with brazen face and impudence, swearing by the might of God: ﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them﴾. Thus the accursed one excepted the servants of God, the believing ones who are preserved, whom God has chosen for His obedience and for proximity to Him in the abode of His honour.

Here God said, in reply to the accursed one: ﴿He said, "Then the truth — and the truth I say﴾ — ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and with whoever follows you among them﴾, i.e., of mankind and jinn, all of them. Here ends what passed in dispute in the Highest Assembly; and how would Muhammad ﷺ have known this and reported it, had it not been a revelation sent to him? Here God said to His Messenger: Say to your people who deny your message, ﴿I do not ask of you any payment for it﴾, i.e., for conveying it, ﴿nor am I of the pretentious﴾, those who invent things about God and say what He did not say. ﴿It is not but a reminder to the worlds﴾, i.e., of mankind and jinn, by which they may be reminded, believe, and be guided. ﴿And you will surely know its news after a time﴾, i.e., you will certainly come to know the truth of what it has reported of promise and threat, and the validity of what it contains of legislation, after a time. Some of them came to know this on the day of Badr, on the day of the Conquest, and on the day of his death.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Condemnation of arrogance and envy, their prohibition, and the explanation of their recompense.

2- The legitimacy of analogy (qiyas) if it is sound, and the explanation of the dangers of corrupt analogy.

3- The legitimacy of swearing by God and by His attributes and names.

4- The explanation that whoever God has decreed happiness for, Satan cannot prevail over them to mislead them.

5- It is not permissible to take payment for conveying the truth and the religion.

6- Condemnation of pretension that leads to lying and to fabricating against God, His Messenger, and the believers.

7- The fulfilment of what the Qur'an reported became evident after a short and a long time.

Here the accursed one, having despaired of mercy, said: ﴿My Lord, then reprieve me﴾, i.e., keep me alive and do not cause me to die, ﴿until the Day they are resurrected﴾, so that he may be able to seduce the children of Adam, and not die when they die at the first blast, so that he would not taste death himself. God knew what he concealed within himself, so He answered him with His saying: ﴿Indeed, you are among the reprieved﴾, i.e., those granted respite, whose lives are kept, ﴿until the Day of the appointed time﴾, which is the first blast, when he will die along with the rest of creation. Thus the accursed one excepted the servants of God, the believing ones who are preserved, whom God has chosen for His obedience and for proximity to Him in the abode of His honour.

Here God said, in reply to the accursed one: ﴿He said, "Then the truth — and the truth I say﴾ — ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and with whoever follows you among them﴾, i.e., of mankind and jinn, all of them. Here God said to His Messenger: Say to your people who deny your message, ﴿I do not ask of you any payment for it﴾, i.e., for conveying it, ﴿nor am I of the pretentious﴾, those who invent things about God and say what He did not say. ﴿It is not but a reminder to the worlds﴾, i.e., of mankind and jinn, by which they may be reminded, believe, and be guided. ﴿And you will surely know its news after a time﴾, i.e., you will certainly come to know the truth of what it has reported of promise and threat, and the validity of what it contains of legislation, after a time. Some of them came to know this on the day of Badr, on the day of the Conquest, and on the day of his death.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Condemnation of arrogance and envy, their prohibition, and the explanation of their recompense.

2- The legitimacy of analogy (qiyas) if it is sound, and the explanation of the dangers of corrupt analogy.

3- The legitimacy of swearing by God and by His attributes and names.

6- Condemnation of pretension that leads to lying and to fabricating against God, His Messenger, and the believers.

﴿And you will surely know its news after a time﴾: i.e., and you, O deniers, will surely come to know, after a time, the news of the Qur'an that it announced: the promise to the believers and the threat to the disbelievers.
